text: The predicate requires B(x,x)∈2ℤ for every carrier vector, precisely the even-lattice condition in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=5). It tests integral vectors rather than all rational ambient vectors. Degenerate and indefinite lattices remain eligible. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L92) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L237) passes.
The rank-one family is even exactly for even Gram entry, distinguishing entries 1 and 2.
The indefinite hyperbolic lattice with odd off-diagonal entries is even.

This is the integer quadratic form x↦L.integralForm(x,x), as in the self-pairing convention of [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=5). The construction uses [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667); it needs neither positivity nor halving the form. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L81) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Norm.lean#L142) passes.
The rank-one integral norm is exactly a k² for an integer representative k.
Its cast agrees with the ambient rational self-pairing.

For each lattice vector, evenness supplies an integer z with integral norm 2z. Casting gives the displayed equality in ℚ, precisely the evenness condition in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=5). The witness is an integer, so this is stronger than rational divisibility by two. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L98) passes.
Every rank-one lattice with Gram entry 2m satisfies the evenness premise.

If all integral self-pairings vanished, polarization over ℚ would make B vanish on the carrier and hence on its full rational span. Nondegeneracy would then force V=0, contrary to Nontrivial V. This uses the self-pairing convention of [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3) and the polarization of [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L65) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L212) passes.
The rank-one family has explicit norm ax², including the degenerate zero-form boundary.
The zero form in dimension one is explicitly degenerate.

Specializing integralForm_cast to the pair (x,x) identifies the cast of the integer self-pairing with the rational self-pairing. Both norm definitions use [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667), so the equality preserves the exact normalization. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L81) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L65) passes.
On rank-one lattice vectors the integer value is ak².
The corresponding rational value is ax².

The quadratic form is exactly x↦B(x,x) on the rational ambient space, using [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667) and the lattice convention in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=5). Negative and isotropic values are allowed; this declaration is a quadratic form and asserts no metric norm axioms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L205) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L211) passes.
The negative rank-one lattice has norm −2x².
The hyperbolic norm is 2x0x1 and has nonzero isotropic vectors.

Evenness of the integer value is equivalent, after the injective cast ℤ→ℚ, to equality with 2z for some integer z. This is the rational spelling of the same parity condition in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=5); the integer quantifier is essential. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L92) passes.
The rank-one parity criterion recovers parity of its integer Gram entry.

Evenness is preserved by addition because the polarization cross term is 2B(x,y), and by integer scaling because norms scale by a². An integral basis therefore suffices to test all vectors, as follows from the Gram description in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Even.lean#L138) passes.
The basis criterion becomes exactly evenness of the Gram diagonal.

The biconditional applies the integer-to-rational parity comparison to every carrier vector. Thus it is exactly the condition B(x,x)∈2ℤ from [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=5), with no claim about arbitrary rational vectors. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L92) passes.
Odd and even rank-one Gram parameters are correctly distinguished.

Evaluating integralForm.toQuadraticMap repeats its argument, yielding exactly L.integralForm x x by [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667). Both sides are integers on the actual carrier; no cast or factor of two is introduced. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L81) passes.
The evaluation specializes to ak² in the rank-one family.

The self-pairing of zero is zero by bilinearity, equivalently the zero law of [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667). This holds for every integral lattice, including zero and degenerate forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L81) passes.
The rank-one formula evaluates to zero at the integer representative zero.

Expanding B(x+y,x+y) produces the two self-pairings and B(x,y)+B(y,x). Symmetry makes the last sum 2B(x,y), giving exactly the displayed polarization identity for [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667). No positivity or nondegeneracy is used. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L211) passes.
The concrete form 2x0x1 retains the same cross-term normalization.

The defining bilinear-to-quadratic operation evaluates at (x,x), so the stated equality is exactly the norm convention of [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=5) and [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667). Its domain is the full rational ambient space. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L199) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L205) passes.
The Gram entry 2 yields 2x², not x².
The Gram entry −2 yields −2x².

On the integral Gram basis, each self-pairing is Gii. Integer combinations are even exactly when these diagonal entries are even: every off-diagonal term occurs twice. This follows from the Gram and parity conventions in [Dolgachev §1.1](https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/idolga-new/wp-content/uploads/sites/1467/2024/08/bourbaki83.pdf#page=3) and [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=5). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L237) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L92) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L243) passes.
Odd off-diagonal entries do not obstruct evenness.
An odd diagonal entry is rejected by the rank-one criterion.
The criterion also accepts the singular affine Cartan matrix.

The even-norm vectors contain zero and are closed under addition and integer scalar multiplication by polarization and square scaling. Hence any ℤ-spanning set of even-norm vectors makes the whole lattice even, as follows from the condition in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=5). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Even.lean#L138) passes.
A finite integral basis specializes this span argument to the Gram diagonal criterion.

Reducing B(x,x) modulo two gives an additive character because the polarization correction 2B(x,y) vanishes in ℤ/2. This is the elementary mod-two consequence of [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667) and the parity convention in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=5); the original integer norm need not be additive. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Characteristic/EvenSublattice.lean#L43) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Characteristic/EvenSublattice.lean#L50) passes.
The character kernel consists exactly of vectors with even integral norm.
Every doubled lattice vector lies in that kernel.

The underlying function of the character is definitionally the cast of the integral norm to ℤ/2. Thus the equation gives precisely its residue class; additivity is justified by the polarization identity for [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667). Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Characteristic/EvenSublattice.lean#L43) passes.
Vanishing of this residue is equivalent to evenness of the integral norm.

This equality unfolds norm as form.toQuadraticMap, whose value is B(x,x) by [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667). It fixes the self-pairing normalization used in [Nikulin §1.1](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=5), rather than a half-scaled quadratic expression. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L199) passes.
The standard A₁ Gram entry 2 gives the rational quadratic value 2x².

The sum norm equals the two given even norms plus 2B(x,y); all three summands are even integers. This is the direct parity consequence of polarization in [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667), with no assumption that the whole lattice is even. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Even.lean#L109) passes.
Closure under sums contributes to the criterion on an arbitrary integral generating set.

Integer scaling changes the norm to a² times the original integer norm. A multiple of an even integer is even, so the stated conclusion follows from [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667); zero and negative scalars are included. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Even.lean#L109) passes.
Closure under integer multiples contributes to the integral-span criterion.

Expanding the integral self-pairing gives B(x,x)+B(y,y)+B(x,y)+B(y,x). Symmetry combines the cross terms as 2B(x,y), exactly as in [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667). The equality stays in ℤ and needs no division by two. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Characteristic/EvenSublattice.lean#L43) passes.
Modulo two, the resulting norm character has the expected even-norm kernel.

Bilinearity gives B(ax,ax)=a²B(x,x), exactly the homogeneity law of [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667) for rational scalars. This is quadratic scaling of the self-pairing, including for negative a and degenerate forms. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean#L205) passes.
The negative rank-one formula −2x² has exactly this scaling.

The integral quadratic form satisfies B(ax,ax)=a²B(x,x) for every integer a, directly from [Mathlib’s bilinear-to-quadratic construction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L667). Integer scalar multiplication keeps x in the carrier, so no rational-carrier closure is assumed. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RankOne/Basic.lean#L81) passes.
The rank-one formula ak² confirms the integer square-scaling convention.

Surjectivity of q:H→H/I makes pullback reflect containment; q⁻¹(0)=I therefore turns q⁻¹(J)≤I into J=0, as in [Mathlib’s ideal correspondence](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean#L70). Published [zero-pullback](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Comap.lean#L147) and [quotient-kernel](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L139) controls pass. This is an ideal correspondence, requiring neither flatness nor normality.
Pullback of zero is the algebra kernel for a surjective coordinate morphism.
The coordinate projection vanishes exactly on the defining Hopf ideal.

For f:H→K, the ideal generated by f(ker ε_H) represents the kernel of Spec K→Spec H, matching [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). Published [all-algebra-valued kernel](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Kernel.lean#L77) and [trivialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L194) controls pass. The ideal belongs to K; the construction needs no surjectivity or flatness.
For every commutative value algebra, the cut-out subgroup equals the point-homomorphism kernel.
Quotienting by the group-kernel ideal makes f the counit-unit morphism.

The equality exposes extension of the source augmentation ideal into the coordinate target, the kernel construction in [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). Published [underlying-ideal](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L78) and [surjective-coordinate](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L94) controls pass. Here map forms a generated ideal; its carrier need not be the set-theoretic image of the augmentation ideal.
Underlying ideal is extension of the source augmentation ideal.
Surjective coordinate morphisms have augmentation as their group-kernel ideal.

Extending the central augmentation ideal yields a normal Hopf ideal, agreeing with normality of group kernels in [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). Published [normality criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Basic.lean#L252) and [point-kernel identification](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Kernel.lean#L77) controls pass. Normality means conjugation stability over every value algebra; it does not require the represented group to be commutative.
Hopf-ideal normality equals normality of all value-algebra point subgroups.
For every commutative value algebra, the cut-out subgroup equals the point-homomorphism kernel.

Forgetting Hopf structure leaves precisely Ideal.map of the source augmentation ideal, matching [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). The published [annihilation criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L145) passes and tests the generated ideal against algebra maps. The equality uses extension into K, with no claim that the ordinary ring kernel of f lies there.
An algebra map kills the generated kernel ideal exactly when its composite with f is counit-unit.

An element with ε_H(x)=0 supplies a generator f(x) of the extended augmentation ideal in [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). The published [surjective-coordinate control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L94) passes, showing these generators exhaust augmentation when f is onto. The hypothesis is vanishing of the counit, not vanishing of f(x).
Surjective coordinate morphisms have augmentation as their group-kernel ideal.

Every counit-zero y in K lifts through surjective f to counit-zero x because f preserves counits. Thus the kernel ideal is augmentation, consistent with [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). The published [identity-point control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L212) passes. Coordinate surjectivity represents a closed subgroup inclusion whose group kernel is trivial.
The augmentation ideal cuts out exactly the convolution identity point.

Extension of ideals composes, so (g∘f)(ker ε_H)L equals extension along g of f(ker ε_H)K, matching [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). Published [containment](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L114) and [surjective-boundary](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L121) controls pass. Coordinate composition f≫g corresponds to group maps Spec L→Spec K→Spec H.
Ideal containment has the direction opposite to inclusion of group kernels.
Precomposing by a surjective coordinate map leaves the group-kernel ideal unchanged.

The first kernel ideal lies in augmentation(K); extending along g gives the displayed containment, consistently with [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). The published [surjective-boundary control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L121) passes. Closed-subgroup containment reverses ideal containment, so ker(Spec L→Spec K) is contained in the kernel of the composite.
Precomposing by a surjective coordinate map leaves the group-kernel ideal unchanged.

Surjective f sends augmentation(H) onto augmentation(K), so extending either along g gives the same ideal of L, as in [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). The published [augmentation-image control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L94) passes. Geometrically, composing Spec L→Spec K with the closed immersion Spec K→Spec H leaves its group kernel unchanged.
Surjective coordinate morphisms have augmentation as their group-kernel ideal.

Killing the generated augmentation ideal is equivalent to φ(f(h))=algebraMap(ε_H(h)), by subtracting the counit-unit value; this realizes [Milne, §1.e](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=34). Published [Hopf-morphism](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Basic.lean#L172) and [point-kernel](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Kernel.lean#L43) controls pass. Lean permits any R-algebra ring A here, including noncommutative A; only the point interpretation restricts A to commutative algebras.
Hopf-morphism version of the algebraic trivialization criterion.
Pointwise unit criterion for the represented group kernel.

Under the generalized-point equivalence, composition with the opposite quotient map becomes precomposition H→H/I→X.unop, as in [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). Published [coordinate-evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L82) and [unop](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Categorical.lean#L58) controls pass. Both sides are the same convolution point; the quotient inclusion reverses the coordinate projection.
Included quotient point evaluates at h as its value on the class of h.
The represented inclusion unops to the coordinate quotient projection.

Applying [Mathlib’s relative Hopf spectrum](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Affine.lean#L177) to H/I gives an affine group object over Spec R. Published [affineness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Scheme/Basic.lean#L77) and [closed-subgroup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Scheme/Basic.lean#L114) controls pass. The same-universe restriction is explicit, and this is the subgroup represented by a coordinate quotient, without any normality or geometric group-quotient requirement.
The scheme represented by the quotient Hopf algebra is affine.
The coordinate quotient induces a closed immersion of underlying schemes.

The quotient projection H→H/I induces Spec(H/I)→Spec(H) under [Mathlib’s relative Hopf spectrum](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Affine.lean#L177). Published [closed-immersion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Scheme/Basic.lean#L114) and [ambient-triangle](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Scheme/Basic.lean#L147) controls pass. Its group-object structure comes from preservation of Hopf operations; no assumption that the subgroup is normal is needed.
The coordinate quotient induces a closed immersion of underlying schemes.
Nested closed subgroup inclusions commute with the ambient inclusion.

This unfolds the inclusion as the image of the opposite quotient projection under [Mathlib’s relative Hopf spectrum](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Affine.lean#L177). The published [composition control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Scheme/Basic.lean#L98) passes, confirming its arrow direction on further morphisms. The equality is of group-object morphisms over Spec R, with the existing quotient structure and no additional choice.
Composition with the subgroup inclusion corresponds to coordinate precomposition.

The coordinate quotient is surjective, so its spectrum map is a closed immersion by [Mathlib’s affine closed-immersion criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/ClosedImmersion.lean#L97). Published [coordinate-surjectivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L146) and [affineness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Scheme/Basic.lean#L77) controls pass. The result concerns the underlying scheme morphism and preserves nonreduced structure; no field, flatness, finite-type or normality hypothesis is necessary.
Every quotient class has a representative in H.
The scheme represented by the quotient Hopf algebra is affine.

For I≤J, the induced H/I→H/J reverses to Spec(H/J)→Spec(H/I) under [Mathlib’s relative Hopf spectrum](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Affine.lean#L177). Published [identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Scheme/Basic.lean#L157) and [composition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Scheme/Basic.lean#L164) controls pass. This is the contravariant inclusion between the corresponding closed subgroup schemes, using the stated ideal containment.
Reflexive ideal containment induces the identity scheme morphism.
Ideal-induced closed subgroup inclusions compose in reversed order.

The equation unfolds the morphism as relative spectrum of the opposite quotient-to-quotient map, as in [Mathlib’s relative Hopf spectrum](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Affine.lean#L177). The published [ambient-triangle control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Scheme/Basic.lean#L147) passes. Both expressions have source Spec(H/J) and target Spec(H/I), so the larger ideal defines the smaller closed subgroup.
Nested closed subgroup inclusions commute with the ambient inclusion.

The coordinate identity H→H/I→H/J equals H→H/J, and contravariance of [Mathlib’s relative Hopf spectrum](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Affine.lean#L177) gives the displayed ambient triangle. Published [identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Scheme/Basic.lean#L157) and [transitivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Scheme/Basic.lean#L164) controls pass. The composition starts at the subgroup defined by J and ends in the ambient group.
Reflexive ideal containment induces the identity scheme morphism.
Ideal-induced closed subgroup inclusions compose in reversed order.

The carrier ideal supplies closure under zero and addition, exactly the additive-submonoid structure in [Mathlib’s semiring ideal definition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Defs.lean#L36). Published [zero-ideal](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Basic.lean#L250) and [ideal-sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Basic.lean#L306) controls pass. The ambient H may be a noncommutative semiring; additive inverses are unnecessary, and two-sidedness remains a separate stored Hopf-ideal condition.
Membership in the zero Hopf ideal is equality to zero.
Membership in the join is a sum of one element from each ideal.

The neighborhood-filter basis expresses arbitrarily small path-connected neighborhoods of each point. The sets need not initially be open; the existing open-basis theorem proves equivalence with Hatcher’s convention. Nonemptiness of each neighborhood is automatic at its point, while an empty ambient space satisfies the local condition vacuously. Compared with [Definition 7.15, p.44](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [§1.3 pp.61–62, local path-connectedness convention](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/LocallyPathConnected.lean#L61).

The source first obtains open path-connected neighborhoods and then uses that each is connected, giving precisely the open connected basis required by LocallyConnectedSpace. This keeps the local neighborhood quantifiers and makes no global connectedness claim. Compared with [Immediately after Definition 7.15, p.44; path-connected implies connected in Theorem 7.12](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/LocallyPathConnected.lean#L197).

A homeomorphism X≃ₜY carries local path-connectedness from X to Y by transporting neighborhoods and paths. The proof applies the open-embedding transport theorem to the inverse homeomorphism, so its domain direction agrees with the displayed result. Compared with [Definition 7.15, p.44; transport of its neighborhood condition verified directly](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/LocallyPathConnected.lean#L181).

Each path component is open because every one of its points has a path-connected neighborhood contained in it. Its complement is a union of the other open path components, hence it is also closed. The local path-connectedness premise is retained; arbitrary path components need not be closed. Compared with [Proposition 7.17 and proof of Theorem 7.18, p.44](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/LocallyPathConnected.lean#L108).

An open subset U inherits local path-connectedness in its subspace topology: ambient neighborhoods at its points can first be shrunk inside U, then refined by path-connected neighborhoods. The subtype inclusion is the actual open embedding used by the proof. Compared with [Definition 7.15, p.44; open-subspace consequence checked directly](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/LocallyPathConnected.lean#L184).

For open F, its path component at x is open in the ambient space. At any point of that component, a path-connected neighborhood contained in F stays in the same component. If x is outside F, the component is empty, so no missing x∈F premise is needed for this openness conclusion. Compared with [Proposition 7.17, p.44, applied to the open subspace; ambient openness checked directly](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/LocallyPathConnected.lean#L86).

The forward quotient map sends the connected-component class of x to its path-component class, and the inverse is the usual map in the other direction. Local path-connectedness identifies the two equivalence relations, so these maps are well-defined inverses. The result is a bijection of component types; no choice of representatives is needed. Compared with [§1.3 p.63, coincidence of connected and path components](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/LocallyPathConnected.lean#L138).

Every neighborhood of x contains an open neighborhood u, whose path component at x is open, path-connected, and still contained in the original neighborhood. This proves that the class definition’s possibly nonopen basis can be replaced by exactly the open sets listed in the conclusion. Compared with [§1.3 pp.61–62, open-neighborhood convention](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf); [Definition 7.15 and Proposition 7.17, p.44](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/LocallyPathConnected.lean#L162).

An open U inherits local path-connectedness, so connectedness and path-connectedness of its subspace coincide. The proof converts both set predicates to the corresponding subtype space predicates. Both predicates include nonemptiness, so for U=∅ the two sides are false and the biconditional remains valid. Compared with [Theorem 7.18 and Definition 7.15, p.44; nonempty convention retained explicitly](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/LocallyPathConnected.lean#L190).

A neighborhood of (x,y) contains a product of factor neighborhoods. Refining each to its local path component gives a product neighborhood that is path-connected by pairing paths. Thus binary products preserve the local property without requiring either factor to be globally path-connected. Compared with [Definition 7.15, p.44, and Exercise 7.4(b), p.46; product-basis argument inspected](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/LocallyPathConnected.lean#L312).

The local hypothesis makes each path component clopen; connectedness then forces the component of any point to be all of X. ConnectedSpace also supplies the nonemptiness required by PathConnectedSpace. Replacing it merely by PreconnectedSpace would lose that required field on the empty space. Compared with [Theorem 7.18 and proof, p.44](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [§1.3 p.63, connected iff path-connected under the local hypothesis](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/LocallyPathConnected.lean#L116).

For each point, a supplied neighborhood basis whose selected sets are intrinsically contractible satisfies the contractible-neighborhood-basis definition. Only indices satisfying p x i need contractible sets; HasBasis ensures these selected sets really are neighborhoods and refine every neighborhood. Compared with [Comparison of intrinsic contractible neighborhood bases and nullhomotopic inclusions, answer 88628; basis reformulation checked directly](https://mathoverflow.net/a/88628) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/LocallyContractible.lean#L105).

Restricting the contractible neighborhood basis to sets contained in an open U containing x remains cofinal in the neighborhood filter. The conclusion retains intrinsic contractibility of each subtype. It does not strengthen these basis sets to open sets or make U itself contractible. Compared with [Distinction between contractible neighborhoods and contractions in a larger neighborhood, answer 88628; cofinal refinement checked directly](https://mathoverflow.net/a/88628) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/LocallyContractible.lean#L118).

A homeomorphism transports a path between any two preimages to a path in Y, and its surjectivity transports nonemptiness. The theorem therefore gives the full PathConnectedSpace structure on the target, with no local connectedness hypothesis. Compared with [Definition 7.1, p.40; homeomorphism transport by path composition](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L628).

Injectivity is unnecessary: for a topology induced by f, a chosen lift of a path in f(F) is continuous because its composite with f is. The source then joins its chosen endpoint lifts to the prescribed endpoints inside their inseparable fibers. This proves the reverse direction; the forward direction is the continuous-image theorem. Compared with [Schmeding, Appendix B.1, Lemma B.2, pp.206–207; noninjective path-lifting consequence checked directly](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/1F5CB46192122ED291D321A762FE4CE3/9781316514887apx2_206-212.pdf/basic_ideas_from_topology.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L466).

The carrier is exactly the set joined by a path to 1. Pointwise multiplication and inversion of paths prove subgroup closure, and the constant path supplies 1. The construction needs neither connectedness nor separation; the group-paper argument specializes to this carrier and its closure proof uses only continuous group operations. Compared with [§4, paragraph before Lemma 11, identity path component as a normal subgroup; broader hypotheses checked directly](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0166864114004404) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L397).

Continuity only on F suffices: every path used lies in F, so composing it with f is continuous and remains in f(F). The image of a point of F supplies the required nonempty witness. The declaration correctly avoids imposing global continuity on f. Compared with [Definition 7.1, p.40, paths in a subspace; continuous-image consequence checked directly](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [Example B.3, p.207, subspace topology](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/1F5CB46192122ED291D321A762FE4CE3/9781316514887apx2_206-212.pdf/basic_ideas_from_topology.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L437).

Every point of a path-connected F can be joined to the specified x∈F by a path contained in F, hence belongs to the ambient path component of x. This is exactly the maximality property of path components. It asserts containment, not equality with F. Compared with [Definition 7.1 and maximal path-component description, p.40](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L499).

For x∈s⊆F, paths inside the path-connected set s also lie in F, so every point of s belongs to the component of x within F. The inclusion s⊆F is the precise condition that allows the same paths to prove the relative component statement. Compared with [Definition 7.1, p.40, applied to path components in a subspace](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L502).

If x is joined to y by a path inside F, reversing and concatenating that path identifies their components inside F. Both inclusions keep the same allowed region F. The hypothesis already forces x,y∈F, so the failure of reflexivity for points outside F causes no exception. Compared with [Definition 7.1 and equal-or-disjoint path components, p.40](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L374).

Pointwise scalar multiplication preserves lp and gives its usual module structure for every exponent, including p=0 and 0<p<1. The proof treats finite support, boundedness and positive-power summability separately. No p≥1 hypothesis is needed for this algebraic conclusion. Compared with [the reference](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2009/01/09/245b-notes-3-lp-spaces/) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Lp/lpSpace.lean#L690).

Continuous σ-semilinear maps form a module under pointwise target scaling. Commutation of the two target scalar actions preserves σ-semilinearity; continuous addition and fixed-scalar continuity preserve continuity of the maps. No topology on the extra scalar semiring is needed for this algebraic module. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/dualmod.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean#L990).

Continuous functions into a topological module form a module under pointwise addition and scaling. Continuity of addition and of each fixed-scalar map suffices for closure. The domain need not be compact and the scalar semiring needs no topology. Compared with [the reference](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2009/01/09/245b-notes-3-lp-spaces/) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Algebra.lean#L585).

Continuous maps tending to zero along the cocompact filter form an additive commutative monoid under pointwise addition. Joint continuity of target addition carries the two zero limits to 0+0=0. Local compactness, Hausdorffness and additive inverses are unnecessary for this closure result. Compared with [the reference](https://math.dartmouth.edu/~dana/bookspapers/cstar.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty.lean#L229).

For each fixed scalar, pointwise scaling preserves C₀ because the target map x↦r•x is continuous and sends zero to zero. The SMulZeroClass assumption is exactly what preserves the limiting value; mere continuity would not suffice. Compared with [the reference](https://math.dartmouth.edu/~dana/bookspapers/cstar.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty.lean#L207).

The two IsBoundedSMul distance estimates lift pointwise to bounded continuous functions with their uniform pseudometric. The first uses the uniform distance between functions; the second uses the uniform distance of a function from zero. The constants remain one in both estimates. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Bounded/Basic.lean#L720).

Each fixed scalar acts uniformly continuously because its distance estimate is globally Lipschitz with constant dist(c,0). This works for pseudometrics and a raw scalar operation, without scalar homogeneity or an assumption that c•0=0. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Algebra.lean#L157).

The inverse of a semilinear isometric equivalence is semilinear for the inverse scalar homomorphism and preserves the seminorm exactly. Applying the original norm equality to the inverse image proves this directly. Separation or an open-mapping theorem is not needed. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/LinearIsometry.lean#L654).

The identity map is a continuous linear equivalence of any topological module with itself. Both directions use the identity function, whose continuity is valid for every topology. Continuity of the module operations is not needed for this particular equivalence. Compared with [the reference](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/morris.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/Equiv/Basic.lean#L270).

ContinuousMap bundles a function with a proof of continuity between the two given topological spaces. It adds no boundedness or compactness condition. Pointwise equality determines equality of bundles, so differing continuity proofs do not create distinct maps. Compared with [the reference](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/morris.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Defs.lean#L32).

The cofinite filter consists exactly of subsets with finite complement. On an infinite type it is the usual proper Fréchet filter. On a finite type Mathlib allows the resulting improper filter, which is bottom; no missing Infinite hypothesis is needed for this definition. Compared with [the reference](https://akruckman.faculty.wesleyan.edu/files/2019/07/Lecture-Notes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Filter/Cofinite.lean#L41).

A property holds eventually for the cofinite filter exactly when its counterexample set is finite. This gives the intended meaning “outside finitely many points” on any index type, without imposing a linear order or countability. Compared with [the reference](https://akruckman.faculty.wesleyan.edu/files/2019/07/Lecture-Notes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Filter/Cofinite.lean#L49).

A fixed point is avoided eventually along the cofinite filter because its singleton is finite. The theorem says that all but finitely many indices differ from x; it does not assert that every index differs from x or that the type is infinite. Compared with [the reference](https://akruckman.faculty.wesleyan.edu/files/2019/07/Lecture-Notes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Filter/Cofinite.lean#L96).

Pi.single gives the value x at its selected index and zero at every other index. This is the usual coordinate-supported function, extended to a dependent family of pointed types. It requires neither addition nor a scalar ring. Compared with [the reference](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Notation/Pi/Basic.lean#L30).

Evaluation commutes with a finite sum of dependent functions, since evaluation preserves zero and addition. Thus the a-coordinate of the function sum is the sum of the a-coordinates. Only additive commutative monoids are needed, with no topological or summability hypotheses. Compared with [the reference](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Pi.lean#L45).

Finite sums are equal when their index sets are equal and the summands agree on that set. Equality outside the summation set is unnecessary. This is the expected congruence law for an unordered finite sum in an additive commutative monoid. Compared with [the reference](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Group/Finset/Basic.lean#L104).

A nonempty closed set bounded below in a conditionally complete linear order attains its infimum. The order topology places the infimum in the closure; closedness then gives membership, while the infimum law gives minimality. Compactness and an upper bound are unnecessary. Compared with [the reference](https://www2.math.upenn.edu/~gressman/analysis/04-evt.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Order/Monotone.lean#L434).

A set of nonnegative real numbers has nonnegative real sInf. In the nonempty case zero is a lower bound; in the empty case the statement uses Mathlib’s real-valued convention sInf(∅)=0. It is not asserting the extended-real convention inf(∅)=+∞. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/m127a_19/summary_topics_127a.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean#L258).

Distance in a seminormed abelian group is the norm of the difference a−b. Negation symmetry reconciles this with the class’s -a+b formula. A pseudometric is sufficient, so zero distance does not silently imply equality of points. Compared with [the reference](https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Introduction_to_Berkovich_Spaces.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Basic.lean#L735).

If the norms of a₁ and a₂ are bounded by r₁ and r₂, the norm of their sum is bounded by r₁+r₂. This is the triangle inequality followed by monotonicity of real addition. Extra positivity premises on r₁ and r₂ are unnecessary because the supplied bounds already imply them. Compared with [the reference](https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Introduction_to_Berkovich_Spaces.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Basic.lean#L107).
